memory_candidates.content: Module placement in a large Lean library is an import-weight decision, not a taxonomy decision, and it should be measured before writing. When a corollary composes declarations from two previously disjoint subtrees, computing each candidate host aggregator's net-new transitive import count separates options that differ by two orders of magnitude: placing a Z-time provability corollary inside the witness-family compression subtree cost +331 net-new transitive imports into an 84-module file and +318 into two downstream aggregators, while placing it in the metalogic directory (which already imported both legs' roots) cost +2, both of which were already in the library-root closure, leaving repository-wide build cost unchanged. The procedure: parse every import line under the library root, compute transitive closures, tabulate net-new modules per candidate host aggregator, and check knock-on hosts such as a separate tooling split that imports one of the candidates. Two standing constraints interact with the result: a generated library root must stay byte-exact against its sorted-import generator, and the aggregator convention requires X.lean beside X/. A suggested placement in a task description is a hypothesis to measure, not an instruction to follow; cycle-freedom is a separate and often easier question than import weight.
